rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Vectors multiply in two ways. The **dot product**, $\vec A\cdot\vec B = AB\cos\theta$, yields a scalar measuring alignment — zero for perpendicular vectors, maximal for parallel ones; it computes work ($W = \vec F\cdot\vec s$), power and flux, extracts components, and gives the angle between vectors via $\cos\theta = \vec A\cdot\vec B/AB$.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - A⃗·B⃗ = AB cos θ = AₓBₓ + A_yB_y + A_zB_z - |A⃗×B⃗| = AB sin θ; direction by right-hand rule - cos θ = (A⃗·B⃗)/(AB) - î×ĵ = k̂, ĵ×k̂ = î, k̂×î = ĵ (cyclic)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Dot vs cross zero:** the dot product vanishes for perpendicular vectors; the cross product vanishes for parallel vectors — opposite conditions.  ·  **Area interpretation:** |A⃗ × B⃗| is the parallelogram area with sides A and B; |A⃗ · B⃗| is not an area.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Dot asks 'how much along', cross asks 'how much around'."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Work*** — W = F⃗·s⃗: a force perpendicular to displacement does zero work.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQ: define dot and cross products with one physics example each (2023, 3m).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Two Ways to Multiply Vectors Vectors refuse ordinary multiplication: $A \times B$ is ambiguous until you decide what you want. The **dot (scalar) product** answers "how much of A lies along B?" — yielding a number. The **cross (vector) product** answers "how much do A and B twist around each other?" — yielding a perpendicular vector. Each has its own physics.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2023) ### 2.1 Scalar (dot) product $$\vec A \cdot \vec B = AB\cos\theta$$ - Result: a **scalar**; maximum when parallel ($\cos 0 = 1$), zero when perpendicular, negative when θ > 90°. - Component extraction: $A_x = \vec A \cdot \hat i$. - Commutative: $\vec A\cdot\vec B = \vec B\cdot\vec A$. - In components: $\vec A\cdot\vec B = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z$.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Dot-cos-scalar; cross-sin-vector — and cross flips sign when you swap."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Find the angle between A⃗ = 2î + 3ĵ and B⃗ = 4î − ĵ.** — A⃗·B⃗ = 8 − 3 = 5; A = √13 = 3.61; B = √17 = 4.12; cos θ = 5/14.9 = 0.336 → θ ≈ 70.4°.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **cos for projection, sin for rotation:** the dot product measures alignment; the cross product measures perpendicular twist.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Dot: A⃗·B⃗ = AB cos θ — scalar, commutative, zero at 90°; examples: work, power, flux.  ·  Cross: A⃗×B⃗ = AB sin θ n̂ — perpendicular vector, anticommutes, zero at 0°/180°; examples: torque, angular momentum, magnetic force.  ·  Component dot: A⃗·B⃗ = AₓBₓ + A_yB_y + A_zB_z; cos θ = A⃗·B⃗/(AB).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The right-hand rule: curl fingers from A⃗ to B⃗ and the thumb gives the direction of A⃗×B⃗ — the same rule that fixes angular velocity and magnetic force directions.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Worked Numericals **Q1:** Find the angle between $\vec A = 2\hat i + 3\hat j$ and $\vec B = 4\hat i - \hat j$. $\vec A\cdot\vec B = 8 - 3 = 5$; $A = \sqrt{13} = 3.61$; $B = \sqrt{17} = 4.12$. $\cos\theta = 5/(3.61 \times 4.12) = 5/14.9 = 0.336 → \theta ≈ 70.4°$. **Q2:** Find $|\vec A\times\vec B|$ for $A = 5$, $B = 3$, θ = 30°.…  ·  ## 4.
